sentences.text: The Vessel Bridge-to-Bridge Radiotelephone Act requires certain vessels on American waters to keep a listening watch on the designated bridge-to-bridge channel, which is VHF channel thirteen in most areas, so that captains can talk directly to each other.

It applies to power-driven vessels of twenty meters or more, vessels of one hundred gross tons or more carrying one or more passengers for hire, towing vessels of twenty-six feet or more, and dredges and floating plant working in or near a channel.
The person keeping the watch must be able to communicate in English.
Most six-pack charter boats aren’t required to participate, but monitoring channels thirteen and sixteen near ship channels is good seamanship.
